subject.title: feat: allow standalone MCP Apps to use bound tools and resources

question: Should a short-lived standalone MCP App ticket be authorized to invoke only its owning server’s app-visible tools and resources under the proposed live-view, lease, origin, and allowlist checks?
rationale: This is an intentional browser-authority expansion rather than a mechanical bug repair; repository policy treats security boundaries and protected member PRs as maintainer decisions.

options.title: Approve the scoped bridge
options.body: Accept the capability after a gateway/security owner confirms the ticket and operation checks preserve the intended least-privilege boundary.

options.title: Keep standalone views read-only
options.body: Reject tool/resource invocation for ticketed standalone views and retain the existing rendering-only isolation model.

options.title: Narrow the capability further
options.body: Permit only a smaller operation subset after maintainers define which calls remain safe outside the authenticated Control UI.

recommendation.title: Approve the scoped bridge
recommendation.body: Accept the capability after a gateway/security owner confirms the ticket and operation checks preserve the intended least-privilege boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the clearest recent feature history across the current MCP App bridge surfaces and can route the intended design to the appropriate gateway/security reviewer.
